newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nippon Oil says gasoline retail prices too low.
newsitem.headline: Nippon Oil says gasoline retail prices too low.

text.p: A price war has pushed Japan's gasoline retail prices too low in relation to the wholesale price, a Nippon Oil official told reporters on Monday.
"Although our gasoline wholesale price for May has been cut, retail prices theoretically should not fall as they are already too low," Fumiaki Watari, managing director of Nippon Oil said.
According to the latest data available, the national average gasoline retail price in March was 106 yen per litre.
Watari said the ideal retail price level for March was 111 yen per litre, including an 18 yen profit margin above the wholesale price and various oil taxes.
He added that more than half of Japan's 59,990 gasoline stations needed more than a 18 yen profit margin to survive.
A price war, triggered by last year's deregulation in oil product imports, has forced hundreds of gasoline stations out of business.
Earlier on Monday, Nippon Oil said it would cut its gasoline wholesale price for May by 0.7 yen to 90.5 yen per litre.
